description: Design visibility and layout overhaul — remove section-level scroll-gating, refactor hero to two-column layout, apply alternating section backgrounds, fix mobile contact form ordering, make services page fully static, and polish hero/HowItWorks/About/Contact layout.

userStories.title: Remove section-level AnimatedSection wrappers from homepage sections
userStories.description: As a site visitor, I want all homepage section content to be visible on load so that I can read the page without scrolling or waiting for JavaScript-triggered animations.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove all AnimatedSection wrappers that enclose entire section content blocks (heading + grid/list together) from: DashboardSection, ServicesSection, HowItWorksSection, WhyUsSection, FAQSection, CTABand
Each section's content renders fully visible on load — no opacity:0 or transform applied to section-level wrappers
CustomerJourneySection motion.divs (SVG animated lines and funnel elements) are left untouched
curl http://localhost:3000 | grep 'opacity: 0' returns 0 matches
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Remove AnimatedSection from services page
userStories.description: As a site visitor on the services page, I want each service section's content to be visible immediately when I scroll to it.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove the AnimatedSection wrapper from inside the ServiceSection render component in app/services/page.tsx
StickyServiceNav and IntersectionObserver logic remain intact
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Fix mobile contact form order and remove AnimatedSection from contact page
userStories.description: As a mobile user navigating to /contact, I want the form to be the first thing I see.
acceptanceCriteria: On mobile form appears above trust signals; on desktop trust left / form right unchanged
All AnimatedSection wrappers removed from app/contact/page.tsx
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Refactor hero section to two-column layout
userStories.description: As a site visitor, I want to see the local pack widget alongside the hero headline without scrolling.
acceptanceCriteria: Two-column grid at md breakpoint: text/CTAs/TrustBar left, LocalPackCard right
Both columns visible on load with no AnimatedSection wrapper
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Apply alternating section backgrounds across homepage
userStories.description: As a site visitor, I want visually distinct section backgrounds as I scroll down the homepage.
acceptanceCriteria: Sections alternate #021524 / #0e2131 in correct order
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Remove AnimatedSection from About page
userStories.description: As a site visitor on /about, I want all page content to be visible immediately on load so that I can read the story, principles, and what-we-don't-do sections without scrolling.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove AnimatedSection import and all AnimatedSection wrappers from app/about/page.tsx
All four sections (hero quote, story paragraphs, principles grid, don't-do list) render fully visible on load
No opacity:0 or transform inline styles appear in the SSR HTML for /about
The principles grid (3 cards with large background numbers) remains correctly styled after wrapper removal
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: navigate to /about and confirm all sections are visible without scrolling
userStories.notes: All four content sections in app/about/page.tsx use AnimatedSection wrappers — this is why sections 2-4 appear as blank space in screenshots. The fix is identical to what was done for the homepage in US-036.

userStories.title: Merge contact page hero into one unified section
userStories.description: As a site visitor on /contact, I want the headline and form to feel like one unified layout with no dead zone between them.
acceptanceCriteria: The contact page uses a single <section> instead of two separate sections (hero + two-column)
The headline 'Book Your Free Audit Call.' and subtitle appear at the top of the unified section, centred above the two-column grid
The two-column grid (trust signals left, form right) sits directly below the headline with no excessive gap
The dot-grid background pattern from the original hero is preserved on the unified section
The gold radial glow from the original hero is preserved
Mobile layout: headline stacks above form which stacks above trust signals (form-first order preserved)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: at 1280px confirm headline and form feel connected with no dead zone; at 375px confirm form is still visible above the fold
userStories.notes: The dead zone is caused by py-24 md:py-32 bottom padding on the hero section stacking with py-16 md:py-24 top padding on the two-column section. Merging into one section eliminates the double padding structurally.

userStories.title: Make LocalPackCard fill the full hero right column
userStories.description: As a site visitor, I want the local pack widget in the hero to be large and visually commanding so that it reads as the visual centrepiece of the page.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove max-w-sm from the root div in components/LocalPackCard.tsx so the card can fill its container
Remove the max-w-xl constraint from the HeroSection right column wrapper so the card fills the full column width
On desktop (md+) the LocalPackCard fills the full right column of the two-column hero grid
On mobile the card still renders correctly at full width below the text column
The SVG map, gold pins, pulse rings, and listing cards all remain correctly proportioned at larger sizes
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: at 1280px confirm the card fills the right column and reads as a bold visual anchor alongside the headline
userStories.notes: LocalPackCard uses an SVG with viewBox='0 0 300 260' — it scales correctly at any container width since width is w-full. The listing cards overlay uses absolute positioning inside the SVG container which also scales proportionally.

userStories.title: Replace hero subtext with one punchy line
userStories.description: As a site visitor reading the hero, I want a concise supporting line that tells me the outcome and method so I know immediately if this is for me.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the existing two-sentence subtext paragraph in HeroSection with a single line: 'Google top 3 for local businesses. Scoped clearly, executed lean.'
The replacement text uses the same className as the existing paragraph (text-lg sm:text-xl text-[#99907b] leading-relaxed)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: confirm the new line reads cleanly below the headline and above the CTA buttons
userStories.notes: The existing subtext is 47 words across two sentences. The headline already conveys the problem/solution. The replacement adds specificity (top 3, local businesses) and method (scoped, lean) in one readable line.

userStories.title: Redesign HowItWorksSection with large display numbers
userStories.description: As a site visitor, I want the four process steps to have bold visual weight so that the section feels premium and makes me stop scrolling.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the w-16 h-16 circle badges with large display numbers (text-7xl or text-8xl font-extrabold) as the primary visual element for each step
Step 01 number is rendered in #C9A227 (gold); steps 02-04 numbers are rendered in white/10 or #99907b (muted) to create progression
Step title (h3) sits below the large number in text-xl font-bold text-[#d1e5fb]
Step description sits below the title in text-sm or text-base text-[#99907b]
The 4-column grid layout on desktop is preserved (grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-4)
The AnimatedProcessLine SVG connecting line between steps is preserved
The section heading 'Simple Enough to Explain in Four Steps' and subtitle are unchanged
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: at 1280px confirm the large numbers create a bold visual rhythm across the four steps
userStories.notes: The circle badges (w-16 h-16 rounded-full) are replaced entirely. The stepDelays array and AnimatedProcessLine component are untouched. The hover state (group-hover:text-[#C9A227]) can be preserved on the number element.
